candidates.context: The PBM device ma y use a light source that is coherent (laser) or non - coherent (filtered 125 broadband lamps or light - emitting diodes (LED)), or a combination of both. PBM is commonly 126 provided by using light in the visible and near infrared spectral ranges, but PBM effects are not 127 exclusive to these ranges. PBM therapy is provided at a much lower fluence and irradiance 128 compared to ablative or coagulating light devices such as those using high power lasers or 129 intense pulsed light (IPL) sources. The mechanism of actions for PBM for different clinical 130 indications is not fully understood. Outcomes are dependent on many factors such as wavelength 131 of light, fluence, irradiance, pulsing paramete rs, and beam spot size. 132 III. candidates.statement: Recommendation : R efer to t he FDA software guidance “ Guidance for the Content of Premarket 360 Submissions for Software Cont ained in Medical Devices ” 14 for a discussion of the software 361 documentation that you should provide in your submission. The software guidance outlines the 362 type of documentation to be provided based on the “level of concern” associated with the device. 363 FDA generally considers the software for PBM devices to present a “minor” or “ moderate” level 364 of concern. PBM devices with software functions limited to an ‘on’/ ‘ off’ switch and/or ‘timer 365 function’ may fall under a “minor” level of concern, in comparison t o a “moderate” level of 366 concern for devices whose software controls treatment parameters. 15 However, new indications, 367 applications, or technological characteristics may result in a higher level of concern. If you 368 believe that the software in your device pr esents either a “minor” or a “moderate” level of 369 concern as defined in the software guidance, we recommend you provide a scientific justification 370 that supports your rationale for the level of concern based on the possible consequences of 371 software failure. 372

Usability Study Considerations for Over the Counter 397 (OTC) Home Use PBM Devices 398 To support a marketing submission for an OTC PBM device, we recommend that you perform 399 three usability studies to 1) demonstrate that lay users can correctly self - select themselves as 400 being appropriate users of the device for the stated indication by reading the b ox l abeling, 2) 401 demonstrate that lay users can correctly and safely use the device after reading and following the 402 instructions for use, and 3) assess the understanding and comprehension by lay users of 403 the patient labeling including all indications, contraindications, warnings and precautions. Note 404 that for cold sore dev ices, s imulated use testing must include information from a usability, label 405 comprehension and self - selection study to demonstrate that the device can be used by the 406 intended patient population without any assistance (21 CFR 878.4860(b)( 7 ) ) . 407

candidates.statement: Recommendation : For PBM devices that can unintentionally increase the tissue temperature, the 506 risk of burning the patient should be mitigated. We recommend that you demonstrat e that no 507 tissue damage will be caused by your device , using appropriate technological comparisons or 508 performance testing data , such as sk in temperature measurements . If your device is likely to 509 induce tissue damage due to inadvertent overuse, we recommend placing built - in time limits in 510 the software or firmware of your device , especially for an over - the - counter device. We also 511 recommend usi ng tissue temperature sensors to detect any potential harmful temperature rise and 512 shut off device output, when needed. 513
